themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints spiked to 6 this week versus a baseline of 0.6 per week—an 860% increase (z-score: 5.42)—suggesting emerging resident friction with the post-pandemic dining shed landscape in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights.
evidence: 6 outdoor dining complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
No prior Reddit or CB discussion flagged, suggesting issue is newly surfacing
reporting_angles: Interview residents on specific complaints: noise, sanitation, sidewalk obstruction at problem dining sheds
Map complaint locations to identify which commercial corridors (Flatbush Ave, Myrtle Ave, etc.) are flashpoints

themes_detail.label: Real-Time Enforcement Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Real Time Enforcement complaints jumped to 10 this week from a 0.9 weekly average—a 1043% spike (z-score: 5.65)—potentially signaling intensified or controversial police/enforcement activity or resident backlash against street enforcement operations.
evidence: 10 Real Time Enforcement complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
1043% spike with z-score of 5.65 (statistically significant, severe)
311 complaint category suggests resident reports of enforcement operations, not official enforcement logs
reporting_angles: FOIL request to NYPD for recent RTE deployment logs and complaint details in CD 302
Interview residents and community advocates about nature of complaints—were they about aggressive tactics, stops, or perceived overreach?

themes_detail.label: Residential Waste Disposal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints surged to 11 this week from a 2.8 weekly baseline—a 300% increase (z-score: 6.88)—indicating a potential sanitation or waste management breakdown affecting household garbage collection or disposal in the district.
evidence: 11 residential disposal complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 2.8 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
300% spike with z-score of 6.88 (highest severity score in dataset)
Heat/hot water complaints (1566 over 90 days) also rank high, suggesting infrastructure strain affecting utilities broadly
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY to confirm whether collection routes were altered, delayed, or suspended this week in Fort Greene or Brooklyn Heights
Interview residents on specific complaint type: uncollected garbage, overflowing bins, missed pickups, or contamination

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bike & Park Rule Violations Spike
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints jumped to 3 this week from a 0.2 weekly baseline (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35), and park rule violations spiked 2 weeks ago—suggesting possible illegal bike dumping or unmanaged micromobility infrastructure in public spaces.
evidence: 3 abandoned bike complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
Violation of Park Rules also spiked to 3 complaints 2 weeks ago from 0.2 baseline, suggesting park-related disorder trend
reporting_angles: Scout parks (Fort Greene Park, Jane's Carousel, Cadman Plaza) for visible abandoned bikes or dockless bike clusters
Contact Citi Bike, Lime, and Jump to ask about fleet management issues or unauthorized parking in district

themes_detail.label: Commercial Waste & Building Use Pressure
themes_detail.summary: Commercial disposal complaints rose to 3 this week from a 0.6 baseline (380% spike, z-score: 4.91), and building/use complaints spiked 2 weeks ago—potentially reflecting commercial construction, renovation, or tenant churn strain on infrastructure during active ULURP/rezoning pipeline (395 Flatbush, Columbia Heights rezoning in progress).
evidence: 3 commercial disposal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (380% spike)
6 building/use complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.2 weekly baseline (380% spike, z-score: 4.36)
1216 DOB alteration/new building permits filed in last 90 days; 395 Flatbush redevelopment in City Council review; Columbia Heights rezoning filed
reporting_angles: Cross-reference commercial disposal complaint addresses with active DOB permits to identify problem construction sites
Interview CB about anticipated impacts from 395 Flatbush and Columbia Heights rezoning on waste and traffic infrastructure
